events.detail: Requirement 14.2 needs the current reporting period and client acknowledgement.
The request is assigned to the project owner with the clause reference attached.
Receipt recorded. The obligation is not verified.
Period, coverage and acknowledgement are checked.
The report covers the period, but does not establish client acknowledgement.
Request the signed acknowledgement. Risk and readiness remain unchanged.
New evidence is on file. The evidence gap is still open.
The new acknowledgement is checked against the requirement and reporting period.
Proof is sufficient. The gap closes.
The action resolves, evidence-related risk is mitigated and illustrative readiness rises from 82% to 91%.

assessor.title: One engine. Different ways to prove it.
assessor.body: Change the framework. Watch the evidence expectations, inspection method and assessment logic change with it.
assessor.disclaimer: Illustrative framework mappings, not an authoritative statement of a standard. Assessor is in development; VAZORA does not issue official certification.

frameworks.name: CBAHI
frameworks.method: Trace the patient's journey. Compare documented policy with records, staff practice and observation.
frameworks.requirement: Care is documented and staff competency is evidenced.
frameworks.action: Request a current competency record and review it against the care activity.

frameworks.name: NCA
frameworks.method: Map the control to configuration and operating evidence. Check whether policy is enforced in practice.
frameworks.requirement: Privileged access is restricted and periodically reviewed.
frameworks.action: Request the approved review and reconcile it with the privileged-account inventory.

frameworks.name: ISO
frameworks.method: Follow a process from requirement to execution. Triangulate records, interviews and observed practice.
frameworks.requirement: Corrective actions address causes and are checked for effectiveness.
frameworks.action: Obtain the effectiveness review and check whether the identified cause was addressed.

frameworks.name: Safety
frameworks.method: Trace a high-risk activity from hazard assessment through permits, supervision and site practice.
frameworks.requirement: High-risk work is authorized and its controls are implemented.
frameworks.action: Request authorization and verify it against the work permit and activity.

frameworks.name: Laboratories
frameworks.method: Follow a result back through the test method, equipment calibration and operator competency.
frameworks.requirement: Reported results use valid methods and calibrated equipment.
frameworks.action: Obtain the calibration record and verify validity for the testing period.

frameworks.name: Education
frameworks.method: Map intended learning outcomes to assessment evidence and the institution's improvement cycle.
frameworks.requirement: Learning outcomes are measured and improvement actions are reviewed.
frameworks.action: Request the review record and map its actions to the outcome findings.

frameworks.name: Social care
frameworks.method: Trace an individual's care plan into service records, safeguarding practice and family feedback.
frameworks.requirement: Individual care plans are current and periodically reviewed.
frameworks.action: Obtain the review and confirm that changes were reflected in the care plan.

problem.title: Contracts are signed with precision and executed with hope.
problem.body: After award, the contract disappears into folders. Obligations live in people's heads. Evidence arrives late, incomplete or unverified. By the time a claim is disputed or a penalty is applied, the proof was never there.

points.title: Obligations without owners
points.body: Hundreds of requirements, scattered across clauses, schedules and amendments — with nobody accountable for each one.

points.title: Evidence that proves nothing
points.body: A file exists. It is not the right file, the right period, the right signature or the right KPI.

points.title: Claims discovered late
points.body: Missing proof surfaces during review, not before submission — delaying payment and weakening the position.

shift.title: Not a document store. A system that knows whether you can prove it.
shift.body: VAZORA reads the awarded contract, structures every obligation, connects each one to the evidence it requires, and evaluates whether that evidence actually satisfies the clause — before anyone asks.

items.a: No. CLM manages drafting, negotiation and signature. VAZORA begins after award and focuses on execution, evidence and claims.

items.q: Is it a document management system?
items.a: No. Files are stored, but the value is in knowing whether a file proves what a clause requires.

items.q: Is the AI Contract Officer a chatbot?
items.a: It can answer questions, but its primary role is to monitor and raise issues proactively — with clause references and exposure.
VAZORA surfaces, quantifies and recommends. Approval and submission remain with your team.
